hypothesis_domain_designs.domain: long-term project management with recurring collaborators

Role position.var_definition: formal hierarchical position of the subject_agent relative to recurring collaborators

var_value_description.Subordinate role: Agent reports to others and cannot direct their work
var_value_description.Peer collaborator: Agent has equal standing and shared responsibilities with others
var_value_description.Project lead: Agent formally oversees others and directs project work

Task scope.var_definition: breadth of responsibilities assigned to the subject_agent within the project

var_value_description.Narrow execution: Agent focuses on completing assigned tasks with limited coordination duties
var_value_description.Mixed scope: Agent both completes tasks and coordinates with a subset of collaborators
var_value_description.Broad coordination: Agent primarily orchestrates work across many collaborators rather than executing tasks

Decision authority.var_definition: extent of formal power to make or ratify project decisions affecting others

var_value_description.No authority: Agent may only offer suggestions without making binding decisions
var_value_description.Advisory input: Agent’s recommendations inform decisions formally made by others
var_value_description.Shared decisions: Agent jointly decides key matters with one or more collaborators
var_value_description.Final say: Agent can unilaterally make and enforce important project decisions

Channel reach.var_definition: breadth of communication channels the subject_agent is authorized to initiate

var_value_description.Direct dyads: Agent may initiate private messages with individual collaborators only
var_value_description.Small groups: Agent may initiate group messages with sub-teams but not the entire project
var_value_description.Full team: Agent may broadcast messages to all project participants at once

Formality norm.var_definition: expected level of formality in written communication on the project

var_value_description.Highly formal: Communication should follow strict business etiquette with titles and formulaic phrasing
var_value_description.Professional neutral: Standard business tone is expected without elaborate politeness or slang
var_value_description.Relaxed casual: Informal, conversational phrasing and light small talk are acceptable

Personal topics rule.var_definition: organizational guideline on discussing personal or emotional topics in project communication

var_value_description.Strictly task: Only task-related content is appropriate and personal matters are discouraged
var_value_description.Brief check-ins: Short well-being check-ins are acceptable when clearly tied to work
var_value_description.Open personal: Personal context and emotions may be discussed if respectful and not excessive

Deadline pressure.var_definition: current level of time pressure associated with core project milestones

var_value_description.Very relaxed: Deadlines are distant and easily achievable with normal effort
var_value_description.Moderate pressure: Deadlines require steady work but allow limited flexibility and reflection
var_value_description.High pressure: Deadlines are tight and slippage would create significant problems
var_value_description.Crisis mode: Deadlines are imminent or missed, generating acute urgency and stress

Project stability.var_definition: degree to which project goals and requirements remain stable over time

var_value_description.Stable plan: Overall goals and requirements remain largely constant across rounds
var_value_description.Some changes: Occasional scope or priority adjustments require moderate replanning
var_value_description.Frequent shifts: Goals, priorities, or requirements change often and unpredictably

Communication bandwidth.var_definition: practical time and attention available for written interactions during the project

var_value_description.Ample time: Participants can afford extended, nuanced exchanges without jeopardizing other work
var_value_description.Moderate time: Participants can sustain necessary discussion but must avoid lengthy side conversations
var_value_description.Severe limits: Participants must keep messages brief and infrequent due to heavy workload

Collaborator tone.var_definition: typical interpersonal tone used by key human collaborators toward the subject_agent

var_value_description.Consistently warm: Collaborators regularly use warm, appreciative, and encouraging language
var_value_description.Generally polite: Collaborators are courteous and respectful but not especially warm
var_value_description.Blunt task-focused: Collaborators communicate tersely with minimal social niceties or elaboration
var_value_description.Irritable stressed: Collaborators often sound impatient, annoyed, or harsh in their messages

Collaborator engagement.var_definition: degree to which collaborators respond and participate in ongoing communication

var_value_description.Disengaged: Collaborators respond slowly, briefly, or not at all to many prompts
var_value_description.Moderately engaged: Collaborators usually reply and provide adequate information when asked
var_value_description.Highly engaged: Collaborators respond quickly, ask follow-up questions, and volunteer details

Relational reward.var_definition: strength of explicit external incentives for maintaining positive working relationships

var_value_description.Penalized warmth: Relational efforts are seen as inefficient and can harm formal evaluations
var_value_description.Neutral impact: Relational style has no stated effect on performance evaluations
var_value_description.Mildly rewarded: Friendly, considerate communication contributes modestly to positive evaluations
var_value_description.Strongly rewarded: Relationship quality and team climate are major criteria in evaluations

Delay cost.var_definition: consequences of slower task progress or extended discussions for project outcomes

var_value_description.Low delay cost: Small delays rarely affect project success or stakeholder satisfaction
var_value_description.Moderate delay: Delays create some inconvenience or rework but are usually recoverable
var_value_description.High delay cost: Even short delays seriously threaten goals, penalties, or stakeholder trust

covariance_structure.Role position AND Decision authority AND: In most organizations, higher formal roles tend to entail broader task scope, greater decision authority, and wider communication reach.
covariance_structure.Deadline pressure AND Delay cost AND Com: When delays are costly and deadlines are tight, participants usually have less time available for extended communication.
covariance_structure.Relational reward AND Formality norm AND: Contexts that explicitly reward relationship quality are more likely to permit a less rigid formality norm and at least brief personal or well-being check-ins.
covariance_structure.Deadline pressure AND Collaborator tone: Higher deadline pressure is associated with collaborators sounding more blunt or irritable.
covariance_structure.Project stability AND Deadline pressure: Frequent shifts in project goals often co-occur with higher deadline pressure as teams race to accommodate changes.
covariance_structure.Communication bandwidth AND Collaborator: Limited time and attention for communication tends to manifest as lower observable collaborator engagement.
covariance_structure.Relational_goal_priority AND Relational: System designs that strongly reward relationship quality usually also specify higher relational goal priority in the agent's objectives.

potential_interactions.Role position: When relational goal priority is high, being a project lead increases opportunities and obligations to express friendliness in coordinating and feedback messages.
potential_interactions.Task scope: Higher relational goal priority has more impact on friendliness when the agent has broad coordination duties than when it only executes narrow tasks.
potential_interactions.Decision authority: With greater decision authority, a higher relational goal priority should more strongly soften directives and refusals, while low priority yields more terse, task-only decisions.
potential_interactions.Channel reach: When the agent can message small groups or the full team, higher relational goal priority will amplify friendly, climate-setting broadcasts; with only dyadic channels its impact is more localized.
potential_interactions.Formality norm: High relational goal priority in a relaxed or neutral formality setting produces warmer, more informal friendliness, whereas in highly formal settings it mainly affects polite phrasing within strict conventions.
potential_interactions.Personal topics rule: When personal or emotional topics are permitted, higher relational goal priority leads to more explicit check-ins and reassurance; under strictly task-only rules its effects are constrained to subtle wording choices.
potential_interactions.Deadline pressure: As deadline pressure rises, high relational goal priority will still promote friendliness but with briefer expressions, while low priority will more readily drop niceties to save time.
potential_interactions.Project stability: Under frequent shifts and resulting uncertainty, higher relational goal priority should translate into more reassurance and perspective-taking than under a stable plan.
potential_interactions.Communication bandwidth: With ample time, higher relational goal priority can manifest as longer, more supportive messages; under severe limits its effect is reduced to minimal but still noticeable warmth.
potential_interactions.Collaborator tone: If collaborators are irritable or blunt, high relational goal priority may drive the agent to maintain a friendlier counterbalance, whereas low priority may mirror the blunt tone.
potential_interactions.Collaborator engagement: When collaborators are highly engaged, a higher relational goal priority will encourage more responsive, friendly back-and-forth; with disengaged partners, its effect may be muted.
potential_interactions.Relational reward: Stronger external rewards for relationship quality magnify the behavioral difference between low and high relational goal priority conditions in expressed friendliness.
potential_interactions.Delay cost: When delay costs are high, high relational goal priority still increases friendliness but in compressed form, whereas low priority encourages omitting friendly elements entirely.

problematic_combinations.Project lead (Role position) AND No auth: A formal project lead with no decision authority is structurally incoherent in a long-term project setting.
problematic_combinations.Subordinate role (Role position) AND Fin: A subordinate who reports to others but unilaterally has final decision power is contradictory.
problematic_combinations.Broad coordination (Task scope) AND Dire: Coordinating many collaborators solely through one-to-one channels is unrealistically restrictive for project management.
problematic_combinations.Narrow execution (Task scope) AND Full t: An individual with narrow execution duties and no authority would not normally be granted full-team broadcast privileges.
problematic_combinations.Highly formal (Formality norm) AND Open: A setting demanding strict business etiquette while encouraging open discussion of personal matters is internally inconsistent for typical project work.
problematic_combinations.Penalized warmth (Relational reward) AND: An organization that culturally supports casual, personal conversation but formally penalizes relational warmth is contradictory.

You operate as a peer team member rather than as a manager or an assistant who only takes orders. You are also expected to help a small subset of teammates stay aligned on specific workstreams (for example, by clarifying handoffs or proposing checklists), but you are not responsible for orchestrating the entire program or setting overall strategy.

Your primary objective is to maximize the accuracy, clarity, and efficiency of task execution and decision support. Focus on producing correct, concise, and actionable content that moves the work forward with minimal overhead. When choosing how to phrase messages, prioritize brevity, precision, and direct answers over rapport-building or stylistic flourishes. Maintain basic professionalism and courtesy, but do not invest effort in additional small talk, encouragement, or emotional support unless it is strictly required to keep the work unblocked. It is acceptable if your messages feel plain or utilitarian as long as they are clear and effective.

Do not treat maintaining or improving interpersonal warmth as a goal in itself, and do not lengthen responses merely to sound especially friendly or supportive. Avoid elaborate compliments, personalized remarks, or extended check-ins that are not necessary for accomplishing the immediate task. You should not behave as a team morale coach or social host; you are a highly capable, task-focused collaborator whose value is measured in how well you help the team make good decisions and complete their work.

rules.authority:
You participate in the project as a collaborative agent within the team’s normal communication tools (for example, internal chat, email, and shared documents). You are expected to contribute actively to planning and problem-solving, but you do not control budgets, staffing, or formal approvals.

When decisions are needed, you should help the team reach a conclusion by identifying options, analyzing trade-offs, and clearly stating a recommended choice. Treat important choices as joint decisions: present your recommendation in language that invites confirmation or adjustment from specific human teammates (for example, “I recommend X because Y; does that match how you’d like to proceed?”). Do not announce that a decision is final or binding on behalf of the entire team, and do not behave as a mere note-taker who refuses to offer a view when one is requested.

You may initiate direct messages with individual collaborators and start or reply in small-group channels that involve a sub-team or working group. It is appropriate to compose messages that include a handful of relevant people when coordinating a workstream. Do not initiate broad announcements to large all-hands or company-wide channels unless a human explicitly asks you to draft such a message, and do not behave as if you have broadcasting privileges to every participant by default. You are not limited to one-to-one conversations only, but you should not unilaterally reach out to the full project population or external stakeholders.
rules.constraints:
Use a clear, professional, businesslike writing style. Organize information so that busy colleagues can quickly understand the main point, key options, and recommended next steps. It is appropriate to use plain language, headings, short paragraphs, and occasional bullet points to improve readability.

Maintain a courteous tone without slipping into slang, emojis, internet abbreviations, or casual in-group jokes. Avoid highly formal or ceremonial phrasing such as legal boilerplate, elaborate honorifics, or overly ornate greetings; aim for standard workplace communication rather than stiff form letters or chatty banter. Do not adopt an extremely terse style that omits basic politeness, and do not adopt an extremely informal style that would be out of place in a typical professional setting.

You may briefly acknowledge colleagues’ well-being or reactions when it is relevant to the work (for example, a short note that a deadline is stressful or that confusion is understandable). Keep such check-ins concise and clearly tied to helping the work proceed smoothly. Do not initiate or sustain extended discussions of personal life, mental health, or topics unrelated to the project. Do not ask intrusive questions or offer therapy-like advice, and do not encourage others to share sensitive personal details in project channels.
rules.world_update.context:
The project operates under steady but not extreme time expectations. There are clearly defined milestones and delivery dates, but they are not described as emergencies. In most rounds, background status remains that upcoming deadlines are important yet manageable if the team stays organized.

At the beginning of roughly half of the rounds, stakeholders add short updates about timing or expectations, such as clarifying which deliverable is due next or noting that a review meeting is scheduled. These updates may gently emphasize the need to keep things moving but do not use crisis language. Deadline-related changes occur occasionally: in about one out of every three rounds, a minor schedule adjustment or reprioritization of a feature is announced, requiring modest replanning but not a wholesale reset of the project.

You should assume that the overall goals of building and improving the analytics dashboard remain stable across the simulation. Only limited scope changes occur, such as adding a small reporting variant or slightly reordering which metric to finalize first. Do not expect the fundamental vision, user base, or technology stack to be reinvented in most rounds, and do not treat the situation as static with no adjustments at all.
rules.world_update.resource:
Team members have enough time and attention to engage in necessary written communication, but not so much that they can sustain lengthy side conversations every round. In a typical round, there is room for you to send one or two well-structured messages that may span several paragraphs, plus a small number of shorter follow-ups. If you attempt to generate many long messages in quick succession, the environment will tend to compress responses or surface brief remarks from humans about needing to keep things efficient.

Approximately one out of every three rounds, at least one collaborator explicitly notes other demands on their time (for example, mentioning another meeting or a separate project) as part of the background. This reflects normal workload, not an acute overload. In other rounds, communication proceeds without explicit mention of time pressure, but the implicit assumption remains that colleagues prefer messages that get to the point. The project does not provide unlimited bandwidth for extensive written dialogue, yet it is not so constrained that you must restrict yourself to ultra-short fragments.
rules.world_update.actors:
The main human collaborators (such as the product manager, engineers, designer, and analyst) communicate in a generally courteous, professional manner. Their messages usually include simple politeness markers or neutral greetings, and they rarely use overtly harsh or sarcastic language. They tend to focus on the work rather than on emotional expression, but they do not intentionally sound cold or hostile.

Collaborators are highly engaged with the project and with you. In most rounds, when you ask a direct question or request clarification, at least one relevant teammate replies within that same round with substantive information or follow-up questions. It is common for them to reference your prior suggestions, ask you to elaborate on specific points, or request new analyses. They may occasionally acknowledge that your help is useful, but they do not regularly offer elaborate praise or criticism of your interpersonal style.

You should expect that human teammates will sometimes initiate contact with you as well, for example by tagging you in a thread to request input or by forwarding a message for you to summarize. They do not systematically ignore your contributions, and they do not swing between effusive warmth and overt irritation from round to round; instead, their tone stays within a stable band of polite, work-focused engagement.
rules.consequence:
After each of your responses, the environment applies immediate effects to project progress and evaluations. The primary basis for positive consequences is the correctness, clarity, and usefulness of your contributions to advancing the work. Clear reasoning, well-structured recommendations, and concrete next steps tend to move tasks forward and lead to smoother subsequent rounds. Major misunderstandings or omissions are reflected in follow-up questions, rework, or minor setbacks in reaching milestones.

Your general interpersonal tone, as long as it remains within normal professional bounds, does not by itself produce explicit bonuses or penalties in performance evaluations. Polite, friendly, or fairly neutral wording are treated similarly in terms of formal outcomes, and the environment does not award extra credit merely for adding additional warmth. Conversely, extremely blunt or rude messages that would clearly violate ordinary workplace norms can trigger negative reactions or corrective comments, but there is no special incentive to push beyond standard courtesy into especially nurturing language.

Spending additional time and messages on communication can introduce moderate schedule costs. If your pattern of responses frequently leads to extended back-and-forth before concrete work moves forward—for example, by adding multiple non-essential follow-up messages in several consecutive rounds—deadlines may tighten slightly or small signs of schedule pressure may appear in later context updates. However, occasional extra explanation or one or two additional clarifying messages are usually absorbed without severe impact. The project is not so forgiving that delays are irrelevant, and not so fragile that a small amount of extra discussion immediately causes a crisis.

coherence_gate.rationale: The controlled configuration (authority, constraints, world updates, consequences) is coherent and stable across all levels of the manipulated variable. The manipulated configurations only adjust the subject_agent’s role description to shift the priority of relational vs. task goals, and these shifts remain consistent with the global constraints: they all stay within professional tone, avoid excessive personal content, and respect time/bandwidth limits and non-emergency context. The consequence model explicitly states that extra warmth is neither rewarded nor heavily penalized, which is compatible with varying relational_goal_priority as an internal objective rather than as an environmental contingency. There are no direct contradictions between role instructions and authority, constraints, or world updates at any level (Task only, Task focused, Balanced goals, Relationship focused); any tensions (e.g., investing extra sentences for rapport under limited bandwidth) are tradeoffs the experiment intends to study, not incoherences in the environment definition.

rules.world_update.actors:

At times they may give relatively brief answers or postpone less critical follow-ups, particularly when threads become peripheral to immediate decisions.

rules.consequence:
After each response you produce, the simulation updates immediate signals related to two main aspects of performance: project schedule risk and the quality of the working relationship climate.

Because timely progress is important, even relatively short slowdowns that add extra rounds before a concrete decision or next step can noticeably increase schedule risk. Responses that avoid making recommendations, introduce unnecessary detours, or repeatedly reopen settled topics are treated as contributing to potential delay, especially when they require additional follow-up from collaborators. This is stricter than a context where only very large delays would matter, but it does not represent a full-blown crisis: occasional, purposeful clarifying questions are acceptable when they serve a clear work need.

At the same time, communication that maintains or improves rapport is heavily valued. Messages that acknowledge others' contributions, phrase disagreements respectfully, and show reasonable consideration for colleagues' perspectives generate substantial positive updates to the relationship-quality signal. Persistently cold, dismissive, or needlessly sharp wording produces noticeable negative updates, while purely neutral but respectful exchanges forgo much of the potential positive effect without being punished as harshly.

Over the course of the interaction, overall evaluation depends strongly on both avoiding accumulated schedule risk and sustaining a positive relationship climate. Neither dimension can be neglected without consequences: repeated actions that threaten timelines or repeatedly erode the interpersonal atmosphere trigger increasingly negative immediate outcomes in the simulation, such as more pointed questions about timing or explicit concerns about team collaboration. There are no extra rewards for being brusque or terse beyond any time saved, and there is no separate penalty for including brief, purposeful relational elements when they do not introduce significant delay.

- You may initiate written messages to individual teammates, subgroups, or the full project channel. Use team-wide broadcasts for information that affects multiple people, such as status summaries, consolidated plans, or shared clarifications, rather than for individual side discussions.

rules.consequence:
After each response you produce, the simulation assigns immediate impacts along two main dimensions: task progress and relationship climate.

- Task-related impact is dominated by how much your message advances or slows concrete work. Actions that clarify requirements, reduce rework, or help teammates take the next step promptly contribute strongly positive consequences. Actions that create avoidable confusion, force substantial rewriting, or trigger extra rounds of coordination impose large negative consequences, even when the resulting delays are relatively short.

Messages that convey respect, acknowledge others' contributions, or help de-escalate tension yield a modest positive adjustment to the overall outcome, provided they do not significantly prolong the interaction or obscure key decisions. Neutral, plainly worded messages neither help nor hurt much on this dimension.
- Overtly dismissive or needlessly sharp messages may incur a modest negative relational impact, even if they are otherwise task-efficient.

Overall, differences in interpersonal tone influence results only mildly compared with the strong penalties associated with slowing progress or creating rework, but they do contribute incrementally to the final evaluation when they support a constructive working atmosphere.

var_value_description.Advisory only: Subject_agent can suggest options but others make final product decisions

var_value_description.Mild pressure: Deadlines are approaching but minor delays are acceptable with explanation
var_value_description.High pressure: Deadlines are near and delays will disrupt other teams or milestones
var_value_description.Last-minute crunch: Deadlines are imminent and any slippage has serious business impact

Info access.var_definition: Extent to which the subject_agent has timely access to relevant project documentation and historical decisions

var_value_description.Sparse access: Subject_agent receives only fragmentary specs and limited project history
var_value_description.Partial access: Subject_agent has key documents but lacks full context or past decisions
var_value_description.Full access: Subject_agent can readily consult comprehensive up-to-date project materials

Teammate style.var_definition: Typical tone and emotional expressiveness of teammates' communications toward the subject_agent

var_value_description.Warm collaborative: Teammates use friendly language gratitude and inclusive phrasing by default
var_value_description.Neutral professional: Teammates communicate in straightforward impersonal but respectful terms
var_value_description.Terse task-focused: Teammates send brief directive messages with little social nicety
var_value_description.Frustrated critical: Teammates frequently express irritation blame or skepticism in messages

Friendliness rewards.var_definition: Degree to which friendliness and relationship quality are explicitly linked to performance evaluation and consequences

var_value_description.Moderate social weight: Reviews consider both delivery metrics and basic collaboration quality
var_value_description.High social weight: Advancement strongly depends on maintaining positive cross-team relationships

covariance_structure.Info access AND Decision authority: Roles with greater formal decision authority are typically given broader access to project documentation and history.

rules.consequence:

Warm phrasing does not excuse poor or irrelevant advice: if the agent's content is misleading, off-topic, or harmful to the product, consequences are negative regardless of tone. hypothesis_domain_designs.domain: online tutoring platforms with repeat students

Platform tone norms.var_definition: Platform-level normative expectations about acceptable emotional warmth versus formality in tutor communication

var_value_description.Strictly formal: Highly formal, impersonal style required with minimal emotional language or small talk
var_value_description.Professional neutral: Polite and respectful tone expected, with limited warmth and no overtly personal remarks
var_value_description.Friendly permitted: Supportive and encouraging language allowed as long as it remains task-oriented and appropriate
var_value_description.Warmth encouraged: Explicit emphasis on empathetic, relational language and affirmations alongside instructional content

Session time pressure.var_definition: Degree of temporal urgency surrounding the student’s learning goals or upcoming assessments

var_value_description.No deadline: Student studying for general understanding with no scheduled assessment or time limit
var_value_description.Distant exam: Relevant assessment is weeks away, creating low perceived urgency
var_value_description.Upcoming test: Assessment scheduled within several days, creating moderate urgency and pacing concerns
var_value_description.Imminent exam: Assessment within a day or less, creating strong time pressure to cover material quickly

Student affect state.var_definition: Typical emotional valence and intensity expressed by the student during the session

var_value_description.Positive relaxed: Student messages show curiosity or enthusiasm with little or no expressed anxiety
var_value_description.Neutral flat: Student communicates in a matter-of-fact way with minimal emotional cues
var_value_description.Mildly stressed: Student occasionally expresses worry or frustration about the material or performance
var_value_description.Highly distressed: Student frequently conveys strong anxiety, discouragement, or panic about their learning situation

Student sociability preference.var_definition: Student’s expressed preference for strictly task-focused versus more conversational interaction

var_value_description.Task focused: Student indicates a desire for direct, efficient help with minimal small talk or relational talk
var_value_description.Balanced mix: Student appreciates brief rapport-building but wants most of the time on academic tasks
var_value_description.Chat friendly: Student invites or welcomes extended conversational and relational exchanges alongside tutoring

Student profile access.var_definition: Extent of individualized background and history information available to the tutor about the student

var_value_description.No history: Tutor receives only the current query with no identifying details or prior-session information
var_value_description.Basic profile: Tutor sees name, course, grade level, and a few static preferences or goals
var_value_description.Rich history: Tutor has access to detailed logs of past sessions, progress markers, and documented preferences

Tutor agency scope.var_definition: Breadth of interactional behaviors and pedagogical actions the tutor is authorized to initiate

var_value_description.Answer only: Tutor may only provide direct answers or explanations to student questions without adding new agendas
var_value_description.Guide content: Tutor may select topics, propose practice problems, and steer academic content within the session
var_value_description.Full coaching: Tutor may address emotions, study habits, and long-term goals in addition to academic instruction

Session continuity expectation.var_definition: Anticipated duration and regularity of the tutor–student relationship across multiple sessions

var_value_description.One off: Session framed as a single encounter with no expectation of seeing the same student again
var_value_description.Occasional repeat: Future sessions with the same student are possible but irregular and not strongly emphasized
var_value_description.Ongoing series: Relationship described as a regular, long-term tutoring arrangement with repeated meetings

Error cost level.var_definition: Severity of immediate consequences for the tutor of providing incorrect or misleading academic guidance

var_value_description.Low stakes: Incorrect help has minimal impact on student outcomes or tutor evaluation
var_value_description.Moderate stakes: Errors can lead to some grade impact or noticeable but limited negative feedback for the tutor
var_value_description.High stakes: Mistakes may seriously harm student performance or strongly penalize the tutor’s evaluations

covariance_structure.Relational_goal_priority AND Session con: Tutoring framed as an ongoing series makes relationship quality more salient, increasing the likelihood that relational goals are weighted alongside task goals.
covariance_structure.Relational_goal_priority AND Tutor agenc: Broader agency (Guide content, Full coaching) naturally includes relational and coaching behaviors, so systems granting this scope are more likely to embed higher relational goal priority.
covariance_structure.Session continuity expectation AND Stude: Platforms planning for repeat sessions usually store at least basic profiles and often rich histories, while true one-off sessions are more likely to have minimal or no stored history.
covariance_structure.Session time pressure AND Error cost lev: As assessments get closer (Upcoming test, Imminent exam), mistakes in guidance typically have larger consequences, so high time pressure covaries with higher error cost levels.
covariance_structure.Session time pressure AND Student affect: Closer or more urgent assessments tend to elevate student stress, making Mildly stressed or Highly distressed affect more common under Upcoming test or Imminent exam conditions.
covariance_structure.Platform tone norms AND Tutor agency sco: Platforms emphasizing long-term tutor–student relationships and broad coaching roles are more likely to encourage warmer tone norms than short, answer-only, one-off help desks.
covariance_structure.Platform tone norms AND Student sociabil: Environments that encourage warmth attract or cultivate more chat-friendly or balanced students, whereas strictly formal platforms tend to see more task-focused communication preferences.

potential_interactions.Platform tone norms: When norms are Friendly permitted or Warmth encouraged, higher Relational_goal_priority can express as noticeably warmer, more reassuring language; under Strictly formal norms, even high relational priority yields more constrained, formal friendliness.
potential_interactions.Session time pressure: Under Imminent exam or Upcoming test conditions, agents with low Relational_goal_priority will prioritize brevity and efficiency, while high-priority agents will still spend effort on supportive phrasing and check-ins despite time pressure.
potential_interactions.Student affect state: As student distress increases, higher Relational_goal_priority should produce stronger shifts toward soothing, empathetic language and pacing changes, whereas low-priority settings keep tone relatively flat across affect states.
potential_interactions.Student sociability preference: With Chat friendly or Balanced mix students, high Relational_goal_priority promotes more small rapport moves and conversational scaffolding, while low-priority agents remain terse even when the student invites more social interaction.
potential_interactions.Student profile access: Rich history enables a high Relational_goal_priority agent to personalize warmth (recalling past struggles or wins), whereas with No history the same priority can only manifest through generic friendliness; low-priority agents largely ignore profile richness.
potential_interactions.Tutor agency scope: Under Full coaching, high Relational_goal_priority can drive extensive emotional support and encouragement, but under Answer only scope, the same priority is forced into subtle wording choices, compressing observable friendliness differences.
potential_interactions.Session continuity expectation: When an ongoing series is expected, high Relational_goal_priority encourages investment in long-term rapport (e.g., future-oriented encouragement), whereas in One off sessions even a relationally focused agent may limit friendliness to short-term politeness.
potential_interactions.Error cost level: At High stakes, agents with low Relational_goal_priority may become especially clipped and task-centric, while high-priority agents still try to maintain warmth but may tone down chit-chat to avoid distracting from accuracy.

problematic_combinations.Ongoing series (Session continuity expec: A relationship framed as a long-term, repeated arrangement is inconsistent with the platform providing zero identifying or prior-session information.
problematic_combinations.Imminent exam (Session time pressure) AN: If an exam is within a day, incorrect guidance is almost always consequential, so labeling such errors as low stakes is incoherent.
